factual_errors: §5 lists 'a Review round-3 technical redesign requires adjudication' as a high trigger, while the same section states 'A role name, round label ... is not a high trigger.' The trigger is defined by a round label.

§2 admits `model_tier: inherit` and `effort: inherit`, but §3/§4 define only integer arithmetic (-1/0/+1) with clamping over the ordered tiers. There is no defined value of `inherit ± 1`, so the calculation is undefined for a legal declared input.

The rejected-options rationale says 'routing is an optimization and can fall back to the main agent,' but §6/§7 admit FALLBACK_TO_HOST_DEFAULT when inheritance is not guaranteed. Host default may be weaker than main, so the stated fallback guarantee is broader than the mechanism delivers.

§7's outcome set has no value for the §2 case where the main profile cannot be observed and no override is ever attempted; §8 would then record fallback_triggered: false with effective_profile host-default/unverified and no valid `outcome`.

§9 asserts 'all four agent frontmatter files', but nothing in the packet establishes that there are four (the evidence paths list two SKILL.md stations); the count is unsupported by the packet's own evidence.
judgment_calls: Model-first over effort-first for complex work is defensible but unproven; the packet correctly declines to claim cost or quality gains.

Mechanical = model -1 AND effort -1 (a double step) sits against the principle used to reject 'simultaneously raising model and effort'. The same pay-once/observe-once logic argues for a single downgrade step. Defensible either way, but the asymmetry should be deliberate and stated.

'ordinary' and 'insufficient-evidence' produce identical routing (main 0/0) and differ only in an uncertainty flag; whether that warrants two classes is a design choice, and precedence makes insufficient-evidence swallow most thin packets.
Keeping the record in active task context only (no committed ledger) is reasonable, but it makes the §10 retrospective style of analysis unrepeatable once a session ends.
Estimating 100–145 maintained lines before a runnable draft exists is a guess; the packet already concedes this.
contradictions_or_non_executable_transit: Round-3 adjudication trigger vs. the explicit prohibition on round labels as triggers, both inside §5.
`inherit` tiers vs. tier arithmetic (§2 vs §3/§4) — non-executable for a legal input.

§6's state machine branches only on 'success' and 'unsupported/rejected routing parameters'. A first-attempt failure that is neither (executor error, timeout, tool failure) has no defined transition; §5 mentions transient executor errors only to exclude them as high triggers.

§2 declares supports_model_override / supports_effort_override with true|false|unknown, but no rule consumes them. A known `false` does not suppress the doomed first attempt; the fields are dead inputs.

§5 escalation defines four ordered causes 'one cause at a time' with no cap on cycles and no terminal outcome when causes are exhausted. Outside the bounded Review episode the loop has no defined exit.

§4 rule 2 conditions on the model tier 'successfully' moving, but success is only observable after dispatch while the rule computes the dispatch profile; it should read 'when the resolved model delta is +1'.

§5 trigger 'the main agent already uses high' is unreachable as an escalation trigger: §4 rule 5 already inherits a main high and §4 rule 4 clamps non-high mains to medium. It either does nothing or silently overrides rule 4.
§3 gives insufficient-evidence 'execute at main 0/0', but §2 may already have forced omit-both-overrides when main is unobservable; the two paths need explicit ordering.
false_downgrade_risks: Mechanical applies two simultaneous downgrades; from standard/low a misclassification lands on economy/low — a two-lever drop recoverable only reactively.

'exact targets plus mechanical verification' is satisfied by edits that are mechanically shaped but semantically load-bearing (renames across a trust boundary, credential or config edits). §3's security carve-out fires only when the requested judgment concerns a security property, which a mechanical packet will not say.
'Crossing multiple files alone is not complex' plus the target-based mechanical test routes broad multi-file refactors to -1/-1.
Escalation cause 3 caps recovery at medium initially, so a wrongly downgraded task needs several sequential rounds to regain the main profile — each consuming episode budget that §7 refuses to reset.
Mechanical downgrade has no evidence precondition symmetric to the high triggers; a single classification error is enough.
false_upgrade_risks: The complex evidence list ('design trade-off', 'evidence conflict', 'ambiguous debugging') matches nearly any review or debugging dispatch, so Review work classifies complex by default and takes model +1 — the more expensive lever — as the standard path.
With a standard/low main, the default Review dispatch becomes frontier/low on essentially every round, and no measurement is claimed to justify that.
Precedence does not prevent upgrade-by-vocabulary: a thin packet that merely uses trade-off or security language can read as complex rather than insufficient-evidence.

The round-3 and 'main already uses high' triggers are label- and state-based rather than evidence-based, and are the two most likely to be invoked in practice — reintroducing exactly the early-high pattern the rejected role-profile option was rejected for.
structured_output.fallback_assessment: Largely yes. §6 removes any user choice of model, effort, retry, or fallback, and the single omit-both retry is deterministic. Two gaps keep the claim from being fully true as written: (1) the state machine has no branch for a first-attempt failure that is not a routing-parameter rejection, so such a case has no automatic path and would surface to the user undecided; (2) the §2 unobservable-main case never enters the state machine and has no bounded outcome value. EXECUTION_FAILED, NON_CONVERGENT, and REQUIREMENT_BLOCKED do end at the user, but those are work-product outcomes, not routing decisions, so they do not violate the claim. Close both gaps and the no-routing-related-user-decision property holds.
smallest_required_changes: Restate the round-3 high trigger in evidence terms ('an unresolved technical redesign disagreement over the same evidence') and delete the round reference, or delete the trigger.
Define `inherit`: resolve it to the observed effective tier before arithmetic, or treat it as unobservable and take the §2 omit-both-overrides path.
Add a third branch to §6 for non-routing execution failure (bounded retry or direct EXECUTION_FAILED) so every first-attempt result has a defined transition.
Add an outcome value (e.g. NOT_ROUTED) for the unobservable-main case, or state that it records FALLBACK_TO_HOST_DEFAULT with fallback_triggered: false.
Add one rule for host_capabilities: when supports_*_override is false, omit that override without attempting it; when unknown, attempt. Otherwise delete the fields.
Bound §5 escalation with a maximum number of steps per task and the outcome recorded when they are exhausted.
Make mechanical a single step (model -1, effort unchanged), or add one sentence justifying why downgrade may move two levers when upgrade may not.
Correct the rejected-options rationale to say fallback goes to main or host default, which may be weaker than main.
Tighten the complex evidence list so 'design trade-off' and 'evidence conflict' require the packet to show the trade-off or conflict unresolved, not merely present.
Reword §4 rule 2 to trigger on the resolved model delta rather than on observed success.
delete_instead_of_expand: §5 trigger 'the main agent already uses high' — unreachable given §4 rules 4 and 5, and it invites a rule-4 bypass.
The '100–145 maintained lines' range in §9, which the following sentence already nullifies; keep only the file-count shape.
`risk_signals: []` and `failure_trajectory: []` in §2 unless a rule consumes them; as written they are declared inputs no rule reads.
Either 'ordinary' or 'insufficient-evidence' as a separate class — they route identically; keep one class plus the uncertainty flag.
§8's closing sentence 'Other routing details remain session-observable, not publication evidence' — restates the section's opening constraint.
